name: Snow Report 2025-11-17 09:10:23
report:
Knock knock, it's winter! The long-awaited arrival of snow came in over the tail end of the weekend, delivering big flakes from top to bottom. Hidden Peak received 4 inches of snow, and the base also accumulated more than an inch. With low temperatures—perfect for snowmaking—and the possibility of more snowfall later this week, Snowbird is fired up to start the season on November 27, conditions permitting. 

On the topic of Opening Day, what are your Thanksgiving plans? Trade in those turkery trot running shoes for a set of skis or a snowboard. The Red Bull MXT Sound Vehicle and a team of Marketers handing out energy drinks will be present to supplement the new season's stoke. 

If you’re a Summit or Alta-Bird passholder who bought your pass before May 14, don’t forget to book your FREE night at The Cliff Lodge, redeemable until December 18. Speaking of Passholder Perks, Pre-Season Passholder Appreciation Day is November 23. Come pick up your pass and get an exclusive passholder shirt (first-come, first-served).

Uphill travel is permitted in Peruvian Gulch, Gad Valley and Mineral Basin.

name: Snow Report 2025-11-17 07:30:00
report:

Forget the turkey trot, how about some pre-Thanksgiving turns! Opening Day is set for November 27.

name: Snow Report 2025-11-03 09:58:45
report:
It’s officially November, which means we’re in the month of Opening Day. So, I hope you enjoyed your extra hour of sleep, because the whirlwind of winter is right around the corner.

This week, the temperatures are starting to drop. At the start of the week, the highs hover around 45 degrees with a chance of snow on Thursday and Friday.

Opening Day is set for November 27, which is also Thanksgiving. Get more bird at The Bird when you make a reservation for The Aerie’s Thanksgiving Dinner. 

If you’re a Summit or Alta-Bird passholder who bought your pass before May 14, don’t forget to book your FREE night at The Cliff Lodge, which can be used until December 18. Speaking of Passholder Perks, Pre-Season Passholder Appreciation Day is November 23. Come pick up your pass and get an exclusive passholder shirt (first-come, first-served).

I recommend taking these few weekends to locate your ski gear and do a recon on all those things you’d said, “I’ll think about this at the beginning of next season.” Yes, I’m talking about the holes in your pants and the fact that you lost your left glove liner at The Tram Club.

Uphill travel is permitted in Peruvian Gulch, Gad Valley and Mineral Basin.

name: Snow Report 2025-10-27 09:31:25
report:
Howdy and happy Monday!

Your summer/fall/pre-winter Snow Reporter, Kolton, here with great news: new snow has arrived! We've picked up 1" overnight, with an additional 2–4" of accumulation possible before things taper off around 3 pm.

Build those snowmen while you can, because sunny to partly sunny skies are expected for the rest of the week leading into Halloween. Make sure your costume is properly layered—highs will stay below 50°, with lows dipping into the 20°s and 30°s. Might I suggest a classic–a one-piece suit, saucer/sled and snow blades… or maybe Ski Bum-bledore?

Looking ahead, Opening Day is just one month away. Turkey Day + Opening Day + Aerie Thanksgiving Dinner = A match made in tryptophan heaven. That's why I'd like to remind qualifying Snowbird Passholders to be sure your Early Bird Cliff Lodge Free Night is booked so you can snag that oh-so-coveted first chair of the season or hold down your perfect mid-day nap zone post ski and feast.

We can’t wait to see you soon.

#GiveMeTheBird

name: Snow Report 2025-10-21 09:16:43
report:
Shimmy shimmy ya, it’s (the tiny) shoulder season at The Bird and we have winter fully on the mind. So much so, snow has been manifested for Wednesday night, followed by some sun, then more precipitation Saturday night to Sunday. Par for the season, we will keep dancing our way through the weather indecision of being cold in the morning and sweating by the afternoon until enough Snowbird passholders use their Early Bird Benefits to book their FREE night at The Cliff Lodge and officially convince the snow gods that winter should be here to stay. Pro tip, use your free night during early ski season, any night from Opening Day through the second weekend of December.

Give me the Bird! Turkey, that is. Mark your calendars, Opening Day 2025 is scheduled for Thanksgiving, November 27. Until then, the Tram is closed for seasonal maintenance and winter preparation. It is all hands on deck getting the mountain and village ready for Turkey Day (also known as Opening Day), so please note that the Snowbird Center will be fully closed starting October 27 through November 1. All outlets, activities, including the Tram and amenities are closed during this time. Bathrooms and amenities will be open and available at The Cliff Lodge for visitors.

Please Note: October 27 through November 1, there will be a planned power outage at The Snowbird Center. All outlets within the Snowbird Center will be closed. Bathrooms and amenities are available at The Cliff Lodge. 

Keep your eye on the horizon for more snow and more announcements about the upcoming season stoke.

name: Snow Report 2025-10-16 08:17:00
report:
Just like that, winter is almost here. Mid-October to late-November is the perfect season for watching your favorite ski movie on repeat (obviously, I'm talking about G.N.A.R.) and waxing your skis in preparation for Opening Day. 

This week expect chilly weather at The Bird, with snow in the forecast and highs in the low- to mid- 30s. Summer Activities, including the Summer Scenic Tram, are now closed for the season. Snowbird's Hiking Trails remain open. 

The Cliff Spa is open from 8 am to 8 pm. For those who want to witness the snow but aren't ready to be cold, check out the rooftop hot tub. Season Passholder Hack: If you bought your pass before May 14, you can still redeem your FREE night at The Cliff Lodge and turn it into a getaway. 

Thank you for joining us for a fantastic summer season and 10 weeks of Oktoberfest.

name: Snow Report 2025-10-06 09:00:00
report:
Fall colors at the base, snow at the peak and the final two days of Oktoberfest are this week. Whether you call it “snowliage” or “fall-inter,” it’s worth a trip up the canyon to see the yellows and oranges of the aspens set against the first signs of winter.

Fall is fading to winter, with cooler temperatures and more snow in the forecast. Highs will reach the mid-50s through Thursday. Starting Friday, both rain and snow showers are expected. Oktoberfest guests should dress for temperatures peaking around 40°. Oktoberfest will return for its final weekend—here's what you should expect. Joseph Toney will be this weekend's live artist, and SLC Pride is the featured non-profit. The daily schedule includes Sun Divide and J-Rad Cooley Band on the Chickadee Stage, alphorns on Hidden Peak and tons of entertainment in the Great Halle. Book a complimentary shuttle ride in Sandy and come on up to Snowbird this weekend. 

Snowbird remains open 7 days a week. Take a ride on Snowbird's Scenic Tram, the fastest way to 11,000 feet—Open 11 am to 6:30 pm. Summer Activities are open Saturdays and Sundays, from 12 to 6 pm. This is the final week Summer Activities will be open.

Take your on-mountain skills to new heights and new places at a discount when you purchase your Mountain School Lesson by October 16. Snowbird's Mountain School offers one-day lessons, multi-week programs and camps with expert instructors who will help you further your on-snow technique. 

Download the Snowbird App or check out the Summer Activities Status and chairlift hours webpages to stay in the know.

Oktoberfest Policies: The festival uses cashless payment systems, no weapons of any kind are permitted and smoking within the Oktoberfest grounds is not allowed. Although we love our four-legged friends, there are no pets allowed (except by special permit) at Snowbird or in Little Cottonwood Canyon since it's part of the Salt Lake City Protected Watershed.

Please note: Uphill travel is permitted in Peruvian Gulch, Gad Valley and Mineral Basin.
